narrative.intro: Techflow is a federal contractor with $310M in obligations in FY2026 to date. The company has 3 awards this fiscal year, with an average award size of $103M, and obligations are up 26.6% year over year. The Department of Homeland Security is the primary buyer, accounting for $310M in FY2026 obligations. Techflow’s work is concentrated in Electronic and Precision Equipment Repair and Maintenance, which accounts for $310M, while smaller work includes Custom Computer Programming Services at $347K and Security Guards and Patrol Services at $5K. Historical annual obligations show variation: FY21 was $193M, FY22 was $247M, FY23 was $223M, FY24 was $271M, FY25 was $245M, and FY26 is $310M. The current-year totals are partial and represent fiscal year to date activity. Contracts listed as largest awards or expiring may show award-value totals rather than obligations. Readers should treat the FY2026 totals as incomplete until the fiscal year closes.

sections.heading: How concentrated are Techflow’s FY2026 obligations?
sections.body: The Department of Homeland Security obligated $310M to Techflow in FY2026 to date. Electronic and Precision Equipment Repair and Maintenance accounts for $310M of Techflow’s FY2026 obligations. Other markets are much smaller: Custom Computer Programming Services is $347K and Security Guards and Patrol Services is $5K.

sections.heading: How have Techflow’s annual obligations changed over time?
sections.body: FY26 obligations are $310M, higher than the prior five fiscal years. Annual obligations were $193M in FY21, $247M in FY22, $223M in FY23, $271M in FY24, and $245M in FY25. Obligations are up 26.6% year over year.

faq.q: How much does Techflow make from federal contracts?
faq.a: Techflow makes $310M from federal contracts in FY2026 to date. The company has 3 awards this fiscal year with an average award size of $103M. Historical obligations include $193M in FY21, $247M in FY22, $223M in FY23, $271M in FY24, and $245M in FY25.
The Department of Homeland Security buys from Techflow, obligating $310M in FY2026 to date. The General Services Administration also appears as a buyer with $347K in FY2026 obligations.

faq.q: What does Techflow sell to the government?
faq.a: Techflow sells Electronic and Precision Equipment Repair and Maintenance to the government, with $310M in FY2026 obligations in that market. Techflow also provides Custom Computer Programming Services at $347K and Security Guards and Patrol Services at $5K.

faq.q: Which Techflow contracts are expiring soon?
faq.a: The FACTS do not list specific contract expiration dates, so expiring contracts cannot be identified from the provided figures. The largest market and buyer entries show award-value and obligation totals that could correspond to active work, but no expiring-contract dates are included.
